$comment: ★★★ LANE-CFG — THE pe ARM OF THIS HEADER, CENSUSED AGAINST THE ORACLE `x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc`. It was reached because `clock()` was UNUSABLE on pe and nobody could notice: `clock_t` had elf and macho arms and no pe one, so the facility failed at the first declaration — the gap hid the gap. FOUR FINDINGS, one of them a LIVE LATENT MISCOMPILE. ★ (1) `clock_t` gains its pe arm. ✔MEASURED: mingw's is `long`, sizeof 4, SIGNED (a `sizeof`/signedness probe compiled and RUN under the oracle) — so `i32 "long"` under LLP64, against glibc's 8-byte signed and Darwin's 8-byte unsigned. ★★ (2) AND THAT EXPOSED A DEFECT THE MISSING TYPEDEF WAS MASKING: `clock` was declared FLAT as `fn() -> i64`, but on pe it returns a 32-bit `long`. Reading a 64-bit return from a 32-bit-returning callee takes the undefined upper half of RAX — a silent wrong answer, not a link error, and it could never fire only because no pe TU could spell `clock_t` to receive it. `clock` is now DOUBLE-AUTHORED: `fn() -> i64` on elf/macho, `fn() -> i32 "long"` on pe. ★ (3) `CLOCKS_PER_SEC` and `CLK_TCK` were declared on NO format, which is what made the facility unusable rather than merely awkward — a tick count cannot be converted to seconds without it. The values DIVERGE and are measured: mingw 1000, glibc 1000000 (both read out of a compiled-and-run probe; POSIX fixes the latter), so it ships with per-format `variants`; `CLK_TCK` is mingw-only. ★ (4) THE SIX pe MACROS BECOME `linkName` SYMBOL ROWS — the same defect class as sys/stat.json's `fstat`. ✔MEASURED: mingw declares `time`/`localtime`/`gmtime`/`mktime`/`localtime_s`/`gmtime_s` as ordinary FUNCTIONS, and a matched `nm -u` control shows what each one BINDS to (`__imp__time64`, `__imp__localtime64`, `__imp__gmtime64`, `__imp__mktime64`, `__imp__localtime64_s`, `__imp__gmtime64_s`) — exactly the `_64` spellings the old macros expanded to, so the BINDING is unchanged and only the MECHANISM moves. That matters because a macro makes `&time` unspellable and changes what `#ifndef time` answers; the corpus witness takes the address of all five specifically so a regression to macros cannot pass. The `macros` surface is now EMPTY and removed. ★ RED-ON-DISABLE, all against the config the compiler actually read (md5 pinned per transition): dropping `clock_t`'s pe arm → COMPILE RED `error[S0006] clock_t`; reverting pe `clock` to the flat i64 → RUNTIME RED exit 2 on the `sizeof(clock_t) == sizeof(clock())` pin; removing the `time` symbol row → COMPILE RED `error[S0001]`; RESTORED → green. ⚠ FOUND AND DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED, with the measurement: `nanosleep` IS declared by mingw's <time.h> and LINKS there, but it is NOT a ucrtbase export (0 hits over 4340 name-table entries) — mingw supplies it from libmingwex/winpthread, so DSS would need a shipped body (~10 lines over `Sleep`, taking the `struct timespec` this file already declares FLAT). `difftime`/`asctime`/`ctime`/`timespec_get`/`_mkgmtime` are declared by BOTH references and by DSS on NO format — an all-format under-declaration rather than a per-format divergence, so outside this pass's shape. | Neutral shipped <time.h> (ISO C + POSIX _r) — c16 (SQLite os_unix date/time surface). SQLite uses time/localtime/localtime_r/gmtime/gmtime_r/strftime/clock + struct tm (it reads tm_sec..tm_year) + time_t/clock_t. ★ struct tm is SIZE-CRITICAL: SQLite stack-allocates a `struct tm` and passes &tm to localtime_r, so libc writes the FULL 56 bytes — a short struct would overflow the caller's frame. Verified against glibc time/bits/types/struct_tm.h + Darwin (apple-oss-distributions Libc include/_time.h — the <time.h> include chain; RE-AUDITED c83 against that exact file: 9 int fields tm_sec..tm_isdst, `long tm_gmtoff`, `char *tm_zone` — the same 11 fields in the same order): BYTE-IDENTICAL on glibc and Darwin (LP64) — `int tm_sec..tm_isdst` (9 ints, offsets 0..32), 4 bytes pad (the layout engine derives it to 8-align the next field), `long tm_gmtoff` @40, `char* tm_zone` @48 → sizeof 56, 8-aligned. So `struct tm` is FLAT (no per-target variant). `struct timespec` is ALSO byte-identical (c83 re-audit: xnu bsd/sys/_types/_timespec.h {__darwin_time_t tv_sec; long tv_nsec} = {i64,i64} = glibc's {__time_t, __syscall_slong_t} on LP64 → flat {i64,i64}, sizeof 16 — UNLIKE sys/time.json's timeval, whose Darwin tv_usec is __int32_t and needs per-format variants [D-FFI-MACHO-TIMEVAL-TV-USEC-WIDTH]). time_t = i64 on both (LP64 signed long). clock_t diverges in SIGNEDNESS only (glibc `long`=i64 / Darwin `unsigned long`=u64) — same 8-byte width, shipped as a typedef `variants` (honest; SQLite's `clock_t x = clock()` works either way). The time_t*/struct tm* params + the struct-tm* returns are typed ptr<void> (standard C pointer coercion) so the layout isn't baked into a signature; the clock() return is i64 (ABI-identical to u64 — same register width). Gated availableObjectFormats:[elf,macho] (the FULL-UNIX-build targets; a windows-pe build uses os_win, a separate axis — MSVCRT time_t/struct tm differ and localtime_r→localtime_s, deferred to that axis). c53 += nanosleep(const struct timespec*, struct timespec*) — both params ptr<void> per house style; the timespec struct (below, shipped c46) is its req/rem. â c82 (shell.c): C89 7.23.1 REQUIRES time.h to provide size_t + NULL without stddef.h; width/value identical to stddef.json, first-wins dedup makes the multi-header provision moot. | c110 (D-FFI-MSVCRT-LOCALTIME-S-EXPORT, the c105-M3 fired landmine that 0xC0000139'd sqlite3.exe): msvcrt.dll does NOT export the bare secure names localtime_s/gmtime_s — only _localtime64_s/_gmtime64_s (dumpbin-verified). So the pe SYMBOLS are the real _localtime64_s/_gmtime64_s + pe function-like MACROS localtime_s(a,b)->_localtime64_s((a),(b)) / gmtime_s->_gmtime64_s (time_t=__time64_t on x64 msvcrt → the _64 secure form is the correct binding; the strtoll->_strtoi64 split pattern). elf/macho keep localtime_r/gmtime_r untouched. | date4.test (per-symbol `library` override, the first user of that field): pe `strftime` binds ucrtbase.dll (NOT the descriptor default msvcrt.dll). Legacy msvcrt.dll strftime is C89 (7.23.3.5) and yields EMPTY output for the C99 conversion specifiers %e/%F/%R that date4's non-Linux format uses, so date4.test -- which compares SQLite's SQL strftime() against the C-library strftime (a fixture Tcl command) -- saw the fixture's C result go empty (expected {}) while SQLite's own C99-complete strftime returned the real string (date4-0..999 red). ucrtbase.dll exports a C99-complete strftime (verified present); strftime is STATELESS w.r.t. the C locale/heap/FILE state (it formats into the caller's buffer and reads only the passed struct tm), so binding this ONE symbol to ucrtbase while the REST of <time.h> stays on msvcrt.dll is safe -- there is no cross-CRT stateful hazard, and the bare time/localtime/gmtime/mktime have NO ucrtbase export under those names so the whole descriptor cannot move (hence the PER-SYMBOL override, not a descriptor-level repoint). The full pe->UCRT CRT migration is tracked as D-FFI-PE-CRT-UCRT-MIGRATION. | ★ RESOLVED — pe UCRT migration PHASE 2 (D-FFI-PE-CRT-UCRT-MIGRATION): the descriptor-level repoint IS now possible, because the blocker above was a NAMING problem, not a missing capability. UCRT does export all four — under its `_64` spellings (`_time64`/`_localtime64`/`_gmtime64`/`_mktime64`, each verified present in the live ucrtbase.dll export table by objdump -p before being added, per D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-EAGER-IMPORT). So `library.pe` moved msvcrt.dll -> ucrtbase.dll; the four BARE rows are now gated availableObjectFormats:[elf,macho] (importing a name ucrtbase does not export would break the binary LOAD at 0xC0000139, since DSS imports every declared shipped extern referenced or not); four pe-gated `_64` rows were added; and four pe MACROS map the source spelling onto them — exactly the `localtime_s`->`_localtime64_s` shape already used above, which is why this needed no new mechanism. ★ THE `_64` MAPPING IS ABI-EXACT, NOT AN APPROXIMATION: `time_t` is declared `i64 "long long"` on LLP64 (the typedef below), and the `_64` entry points are precisely the 64-bit-`__time64_t` variants — so signature, width and semantics all match. Had time_t been 32-bit here, this mapping would have been a silent-corruption bug rather than a fix. The `strftime` PER-SYMBOL override is RETIRED by this phase: it pointed at ucrtbase.dll to dodge legacy msvcrt's C89 strftime (the date4.test 1000-failure cluster), and the descriptor default is now that same image, so the override became a no-op restating the default — the first of the surgical patches this migration exists to remove. Co-state note: `localtime`/`gmtime` return a pointer into the CRT's STATIC `tm` buffer, which is per-runtime state — but it is a plain POD struct, not an opaque handle, so a `tm*` produced by one CRT and merely READ by another is safe (that is exactly why the strftime override worked while the rest of this descriptor was still msvcrt). That is why time.json is its own phase rather than a member of the P3 stateful co-state group (heap/FILE*/fd/errno), whose objects DO carry runtime-owned identity.
